clue.text: About to crack? This may be called for

definitions.text: About to crack? This may be called for

parts.note: RE is Latin-derived 'regarding', a standard crossword 'about'
to crack a puzzle or code is to solve it

explanation.surface: Someone on the verge of a breakdown is told what they will need to hold together.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the wordplay reads 'about' plus 'crack', and the full sentence says that firmness of purpose is what you need when close to breaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve is determination, the quality a person close to breaking down must summon.

clue.text: German banker's text to personnel to identify themselves?

parts.note: text-speak R U is 'are you', asking someone who they are
HR is human resources, the personnel department
says what the text asks; it gives no letters

explanation.surface: A German bank employee sends a message asking staff to confirm who they are.
explanation.walkthrough: A banker in crosswords is a river, something with banks; the Ruhr is a river in western Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ruhr is a German river, and a river is a thing with banks.

clue.text: Dog delivering bite, after jumping up, that is

parts.note: something sharp has a bite, as a sharp taste or remark does

indicators.note: in a down answer, jumping up means the letters go upward, read in reverse

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A dog that bites someone after leaping up at them.
explanation.definitionFit: The shar pei is a Chinese breed of dog known for its wrinkled skin.

clue.text: Going topless, lit up fundraiser

indicators.note: topless means without its top, so in a down answer the first letter goes

parts.note: blotto and lit up are both slang for very drunk

explanation.surface: A drunken topless reveller at a charity event.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotto is a lottery, a game of chance often run to raise funds.

clue.text: Intrude by stealth, or chance, after straying

indicators.note: straying means wandering off course, so the letters wander out of their order

parts.note: taken as written, eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks in, perhaps by luck, after wandering off.
explanation.definitionFit: To encroach is to advance gradually beyond proper limits, intruding by stealth.

clue.text: Give in short extract with book

indicators.note: something short is missing its end, so the final letter of the word for extract is cut

parts.note: to suck out is to extract, as sap is drawn; the verb loses its last letter
cum is Latin for with, as in a kitchen-cum-diner
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: An instruction to surrender a brief excerpt along with a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: Cum, Latin for with, is familiar from English compounds like bedroom-cum-study.
explanation.definitionFit: To succumb is to yield or surrender, which is what giving in means.

clue.text: Irish-born novelist back on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means something heard broadcast, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: An Irish-born writer returns to broadcasting.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Sterne, author of Tristram Shandy, was born in Clonmel in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was an eighteenth-century novelist born in Ireland.

clue.text: Male casualty in US I look after

parts.note: a chap is a man
ER, emergency room, is the American term for a casualty department
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man injured in America announces he will care for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Casualty is the British name for a hospital's emergency department, so its US equivalent is ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To chaperone is to accompany and supervise someone, looking after them.

clue.text: Lots of egg shell's left at the end of the day

indicators.note: the shell has left, so the outer letters of the egg's name are gone

parts.note: Humpty Dumpty is the egg of the nursery rhyme
e'en is a poetic contraction of evening

explanation.surface: A lot of eggshell is left over by evening.
explanation.walkthrough: Shell's left is read as 'the shell has gone', not as something remaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteen is informal for very many, an indefinitely large number, so lots of.

clue.text: Like Abba's ratings in a two-part series?

definitions.text: Like Abba's ratings in a two-part series?

parts.note: setter's reading: ratings are AB sailors, and the band's name is AB and BA placed spine to spine
surface reading: a TV show's viewing figures, top in consecutive episodes

explanation.walkthrough: Ratings are ordinary seamen, abbreviated AB, and the band name is two of them facing opposite ways; consecutive hits are also this.
explanation.definitionFit: Back-to-back means consecutive, one after another, and also describes two things facing in opposite directions.

clue.text: Gather whiskers responsible for pain

parts.note: to gather news is to hear of it
a tache is short for moustache

explanation.surface: Collecting facial hair turns out to be the cause of suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional anguish, a kind of pain.

clue.text: Food that might wobble when still?

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a still is a photograph, a pic

explanation.surface: A riddle about a dish that trembles even when motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' wants to mean motionless, making a paradox; it is a noun, a single photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from stock, a food that sets and quivers on the plate.

clue.text: Declaration that binds me and you together, for example?

parts.note: 'me' and 'you' are each an instance of this part of speech
binds, read with 'together', is what cement does
completes 'binds together'; it gives no letters
marks 'me and you' as examples of a class; it gives no letters

explanation.surface: A statement that joins two people, perhaps a wedding vow.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'binds together' is split around 'me and you', and 'for example' marks 'me and you' as instances of a grammatical class.
explanation.definitionFit: A pronouncement is a formal statement or announcement, so a declaration.

clue.text: A say in revamp of pub: good role, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter of the final word is dropped
a revamp is a makeover, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the word without its final letter

explanation.surface: Having some say in the refurbishment of a pub is a good role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A say' reads as having a voice, but it is the letter A given as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A is one of the ABO blood groups, so 'A, say' is an example defining the category.

clue.text: Relaxed, having large charity to support

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
aid is help given as charity
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A calm person who has a big good cause to fund.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid-back is informal for easy-going, an idiom for being relaxed.

clue.text: Navy fur wraps to acquire as new?

indicators.note: wraps means encloses, so the fur stole goes around the other piece

parts.note: a boa is a fur or feather stole
RN is the Royal Navy
to gain is to acquire

explanation.surface: A navy-blue fur coat wrapped up to look new.
explanation.definitionFit: Born-again describes someone renewed, as if made new, especially by religious conversion.

clue.text: Keep company's top of the range Datsun, finally passed on

parts.note: a range is a kitchen stove, and the hob is its top

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the car maker's name

parts.note: the last letter of Datsun
OB, Latin obiit, means died, i.e. passed on

explanation.surface: A firm's flagship car model is said to have been sold or discontinued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top of the range' looks like sales talk for the best model, but a range is a cooking stove here.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to socialise or mix familiarly, keeping company with others.

clue.text: Section of canal carrying warning on subject of tug?

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout
a lock is a gated section of a canal

explanation.surface: A canal tugboat passing through a lock with a warning sign.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, the lock carrying the warning has the warning on top. Tugging the forelock was a servant's gesture of deference.
explanation.definitionFit: A forelock is the lock of hair over the brow, traditionally tugged as a sign of respect.

clue.text: Man abandoning plot for all his books?

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so the first word is taken out of the second

parts.note: a manoeuvre is a scheme or plot
taken as written, the part removed

explanation.surface: A writer gives up on a storyline, and that is his whole output.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the man from the scheming word and the French term for a body of work remains.
explanation.definitionFit: An oeuvre is the complete body of a writer's or artist's work; the question mark marks the books as one example.

clue.text: Bath for one slow to remove last item of clothing

indicators.note: remove last says the final letter is taken away from the word for slow

parts.note: Bath has a university, so it is one example of a uni
tardy means slow or late

explanation.surface: A slow bather is told to take off a final garment.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath looks like a tub, but it is the English city with a university.
explanation.definitionFit: A unitard is a one-piece skin-tight garment covering body and legs, worn by dancers and gymnasts.

clue.text: Row of houses?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a quarrel, rhyming with cow, especially one at home
second meaning: relating to the home or household

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a terrace of houses, but splits into a noun for a household quarrel and an adjective meaning of the home.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic is British slang for a quarrel at home, and as an adjective the word means belonging to the household.

clue.text: Acrobatic little singers etc exercised with it while holding note

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so the musical syllable sits within
exercised suggests being put through movements, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Small songbirds and the like doing gymnastic routines while sustaining a note.
explanation.definitionFit: Titmice are small agile songbirds that often hang upside down when feeding, hence acrobatic.

clue.text: Police officer happy after promotion? Makes sense

indicators.note: after places the officer and the mood behind the advertising word in the final order

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a promotion
DS is a detective sergeant
up means in high spirits

explanation.surface: An officer pleased to have been promoted, which is logical.
explanation.walkthrough: Promotion looks like a rise in rank for the officer, but it is an advertisement placed before the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that adds up is consistent and logical, so it makes sense.

clue.text: Endure the unpleasant cocktail that's consumed right across Russia

indicators.note: something consumed is taken inside, so the cocktail swallows the other parts

parts.note: gin and it is gin with Italian vermouth
R is the abbreviation for right
the bear is the traditional emblem of Russia

explanation.surface: A drinker puts up with a nasty mixed drink that is drunk all over Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: The cocktail takes in two separate pieces at different points; 'it' in gin and it is short for Italian vermouth, and the bear stands for Russia as its national emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: To grin and bear it is the idiom for putting up with something unpleasant without complaint.

clue.text: Yard, with men, has turned riotous

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the assembled letters are read backwards

parts.note: YD is the abbreviation for yard
W is the abbreviation for with
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A yard full of men has become a scene of disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdy means noisy and disorderly, as riotous behaviour is.

clue.text: Kid in France I found on street

parts.note: je is French for I
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A child in France was discovered out on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: Kid looks like a noun for a child, but it is the verb to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid is to tease or joke, and a jest is a joke, so both share the playful sense; jest is also a verb meaning to kid.

clue.text: Port kept in oak, as originally recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read in the reverse direction
kept in says the letters are held inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across 'oak', 'as' and the start of 'originally'

explanation.surface: A fortified wine stored in oak barrels, as it was first remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: Port looks like the drink stored in oak casks, but it is a harbour city in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major Japanese seaport on Osaka Bay.

clue.text: Whose twin somehow is never spotted

indicators.note: somehow suggests an unspecified way of rearranging, so the letters get reordered

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A puzzle about someone whose identical sibling is never seen.
explanation.walkthrough: Spotted wants to mean seen, but it means marked with spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow-white means pure white, so free of any mark or stain, never spotted.

clue.text: Dickensian school match!

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
snap is the card game of matching pairs, and a call when two match

explanation.surface: A school sports fixture written up in the manner of Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Podsnap is the smug, self-satisfied character in Dickens's Our Mutual Friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Podsnap is a character created by Dickens, so a Dickensian figure.

clue.text: US island escape? Initially wonderful time there!

parts.note: Escape is a key on a computer keyboard

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the first letter of wonderful
Eastern Standard Time, the time zone used in Florida

explanation.surface: A getaway to an American island promises a great holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Escape looks like a holiday but is the keyboard key, and 'time there' means the local time zone.
explanation.definitionFit: Key West is an island at the southern tip of the Florida Keys in the US.
